subject: bin2d or similar, with fill aesthetic proportional to percentage _within each vertical strip_

messages.author: aa972b696d7a0927
messages.subject: bin2d or similar, with fill aesthetic proportional to percentage _within each vertical strip_
parts:
The fill aesthetic in geom_bin2d defaults to 'count', which is the
number of cases in each individual rectangle. You can use
aes(fill=..density..) instead, but that just divides each rectangle by
the total count, so it doesn't change the appearance of the plot at
all, only the value range on the colorbar.

What would I have to do to get the fill to be proportional to the
density within _each vertical strip considered by itself_? That might
be easier to understand with an example: given prebinned data

test.d <- data.frame(x=c(1,1,1,2,2,2,3,3,3), y=c(1,2,3,1,2,3,1,2,3),
count=c(12,6,3,4,2,0,1,0,0))

fill=..density.. effectively does

test.d$density <- test.d$count / sum(test.d$count)

but the calculation I want is

test.d$v.density <- ddply(test.d, .(x), function(blk)
data.frame(v.density=blk$count / sum(blk$count)))$v.density

However, I do _not_ have pre-binned data so I need to persuade
stat_bin2d to do that somehow.

zw
